usageNotes: Appends a new firewall rule to the VM-level ruleset; the VM's firewall must be enabled (via the VM firewall options) and the cluster/node firewall must also be active for rules to take effect. Requires VM.Config.Network on /vms/{vmid}. The rule is appended to the end of the list unless 'pos' is specified; use 'pos' carefully — rules are evaluated in order and an incorrect position can silently shadow or be shadowed by existing rules.

examples.summary: Block all inbound traffic on port 3389 (RDP) from the internet to a Windows VM

params.comment: Block inbound RDP from all sources

tips: Use 'macro' (e.g., 'SSH', 'HTTP', 'HTTPS') instead of manually specifying proto+dport when a standard macro exists — it reduces errors and improves readability.
Pass 'digest' from a prior GET of the ruleset to guard against concurrent modifications overwriting each other.
Rules apply per-VM and are independent of node-level or cluster-level firewall rules; all three layers stack.
The 'iface' param for VMs must match a VM network key like 'net0', 'net1', etc. — not a host interface name.
A rule with 'enable': 0 is saved but inactive; useful for staging rules before activating them.
